solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Incantation you heard in Bond film?

parts.note: an incantation is a magic spell

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the name Bond

parts.note: taken as written: James Bond's surname

indicators.note: heard tells us the word you is taken as it is spoken, a single letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone hears a magic incantation spoken during a James Bond movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond film' looks like the definition, but Bond is wordplay; the definition is just 'film?', the question mark warning it is one particular film.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound is a 1945 Alfred Hitchcock thriller starring Ingrid Bergman and Gregory Peck.

clue.text: Capital girl raised to support struggle

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece supports the one placed above it

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the name is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from a capital city is brought up to support some struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts the reversed girl's name (NNA, from 'raised') below VIE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Got it after bar reduced champagne

indicators.note: after places the radio acknowledgement following the shortened bar
reduced means the word for bar loses its final letter

parts.note: a pole is a long bar
Roger is radio language for 'message received, got it'

explanation.surface: Someone understood the message once the bar had cut its champagne prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got it' is radio-operator jargon for message received; 'reduced' trims the last letter of the bar, and 'after' sets the radio word second.
explanation.definitionFit: Pol Roger is a well-known French champagne house, and its wine carries that brand name.

clue.text: Composer from northern part of Berlin (Germany's capital)

indicators.note: in a down answer the northern part is the top, so only the opening stretch of the city name is kept
a capital letter is the first one, so take the initial of Germany

explanation.surface: A composer comes from the northern districts of the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern part of' keeps BER from Berlin (the top in a down entry); 'capital' gives G, the first letter of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, known for the opera Wozzeck.

clue.text: What may be added to drink, drop of red in drinking mug or vessel?

parts.words: What may be added to drink
parts.note: ice is often added to a drink

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for a drinking mug

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking cup or mug

indicators.note: a drop of something is just a little of it, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail question: add ice, or a drop of red wine poured into a mug?
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop of' gives R, the first letter of red, which 'in' puts inside BEAKER to make BREAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a ship built to clear a passage through frozen seas; the question mark flags the pun on ice.

clue.text: Cutting a new chequered cloth

parts.note: a cutting remark is a tart, sharp one

explanation.surface: Scissors are cutting a new length of checked fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as snipping with scissors, but here it is an adjective, as in a sharp, tart remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the woollen fabric woven in a crisscross check pattern, associated with Scottish clans.

clue.text: Fruit stack in Irish port

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a rick is a stack of hay or straw

explanation.surface: A pile of fruit is stacked up on the quay at an Irish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Limerick is a city and port on the River Shannon in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Article put in study for college administrator

indicators.note: put in tells us the article goes inside the word for a study

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article has been placed in the study belonging to a college official.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior official in a college or university who runs a faculty or student discipline.

clue.text: Police (CID) has one moving thing likely to become a problem

definitions.text: thing likely to become a problem

indicators.note: moving means these letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: The police's detective branch is relocating someone, a move likely to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges all the letters of POLICE, CID, HAS and ONE. CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is an apparently attractive job or gift that turns out to bring trouble.

clue.text: Ship's course close to Dover

parts.note: a line is a course or route followed

indicators.note: close means end here, so the last letter of Dover is taken

explanation.surface: A ship's route takes it close in to Dover, the Channel port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearness, but it means the end of Dover, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship sailing on a regular route.

clue.text: Start to back small northern broker

parts.note: go can mean a start, as in ready, steady, go
to bet on something is to back it
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone begins backing a small broker based in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who negotiates for others, just as a broker arranges deals.

clue.text: Sweetheart gets upset about ending in crime novel

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or sweetheart

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters go around another piece
upset means the letters of gets are knocked into a new order
the ending of crime is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lover is distressed over the ending of a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges GETS as GSTE, and 'about' puts that around E, the last letter of crime ('ending in'), to make GESTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is P. C. Wren's 1924 adventure novel about brothers in the French Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Chat with female during landmark duel

indicators.note: during puts the chat and the female within the landmark

parts.note: a sight is a landmark that tourists come to see
to have a word with someone is to chat

explanation.surface: Someone chats with a woman while visiting a famous landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places WORDF inside SIGHT, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, classically conducted with swords.

clue.text: Nymph? No, a wizard, oddly

parts.note: N is a short form of no, as in a Y/N box

indicators.note: oddly signals that letters are taken alternately from wizard

explanation.surface: Asked whether she is a nymph, she says no, she is an oddly behaving wizard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' here takes the alternate letters I, A, D from wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek mythology who lives in a river, spring or lake.

clue.text: Opera company, from year dot, dotty about Lyceum? Not half!

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters wrap around another piece
dotty means crazy, so the letters of year and dot are jumbled
not half means only half the word Lyceum is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: An opera company has been crazy about a famous theatre since the year dot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' scrambles the year-dot letters and 'about' wraps them round the half that 'Not half' keeps of Lyceum, a London theatre. 'The year dot' means a very long time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The D'Oyly Carte Opera Company has long staged the comic operas of Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: Below, clue involving rugby player also inside

indicators.note: involving here links the clue word with the player and the word for also, joined together

parts.note: under means below
a lock is a forward in the second row of a rugby scrum
and means also
a key is a clue to a puzzle

explanation.surface: A clue below somehow involves a rugby player too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' simply joins KEY with LOCK AND; the pieces are set down in the order UNDER, LOCK, AND, KEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept under lock and key is locked up in prison, which is slang for being inside.

clue.text: Ignore reduction

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to disregard it

explanation.surface: Disregard the price cut.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb discount means to dismiss as unimportant; as a noun it is a deduction from the usual price.

clue.text: Finer points of French resort site after redevelopment

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: redevelopment of the site means its letters are rebuilt into another order

explanation.surface: The finer details of a French Riviera resort site once it has been redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the Riviera resort, not the adjective; 'after redevelopment' signals that the site's letters are rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine distinctions or subtle details, the delicate points of a matter.

clue.text: Attractive daughter retiring around one

indicators.note: around means those letters are placed round the one

parts.note: a retiring person is shy and reserved
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An attractive daughter is shy around a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like a reversal, but it means shy; 'around' puts D and SHY round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for good-looking or sexually attractive.

clue.text: Betsey at last names corrupt Uriah Heep, for one

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of Betsey is taken
corrupt means the letters of names are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Betsey Trotwood finally names the corrupt clerk Uriah Heep, both from David Copperfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives Y from Betsey; 'corrupt' rearranges NAMES as ESMAN. Betsey Trotwood and Uriah Heep are both characters in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is Dickens's fawning, obsequious clerk, an example of a sycophant who always agrees.

clue.text: Guide, Diane, in front of minister's house

indicators.note: in front of places the short name before the house

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane
a rectory is the house of a rector, a church minister

explanation.surface: Diane guides visitors from in front of the vicar's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a reference book listing names and addresses, serving as a guide.

clue.text: Grease equipment in drilling installation

parts.note: to oil something is to grease it
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Machinery is being greased on an offshore drilling platform.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is the structure that drills wells for petroleum, at sea or on land.

clue.text: Lively exchange of opinions may make one irritable ahead of launch

indicators.note: ahead of puts the irritable word before the launch word

parts.note: cross means irritable or annoyed
to fire a missile is to launch it

explanation.surface: An argument might leave a person cross just before a rocket launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is a heated exchange of comments, by extension from gunfire crossing from several directions.

clue.text: Secret language, chapter and verse

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A cipher hidden in the chapter and verse of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chapter and verse' looks like a single idiom for exact detail, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a system of symbols used to keep messages secret.

clue.text: Advantage of golf club excluding women

indicators.note: excluding tells us the women's letter is removed from the club

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club that bars women gains an unfair advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls male-only golf clubs; the club here is the iron, not the institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge means holding an advantage over a rival.

clue.text: Time left in American city

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the American letters

parts.note: American is represented by USA

explanation.surface: Time is running out in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American city' looks like the definition; American is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma, on the Arkansas River.

clue.text: Teeth: sign in lady for treatment from me, perhaps

indicators.note: treatment works on the letters here, reshaping them into a new order

explanation.surface: A notice on the teeth asks the lady to sign in for her treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' rearranges TEETH SIGN IN LADY. The definition makes the answer the speaker: the person giving the treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental hygienist cleans and treats patients' teeth, and is the 'me' who might speak this clue.
